The proposal expressly distinguishes historical homeland description from present reservation boundaries and legal jurisdiction. No coordinates, title, acreage, treaty rights or legal outcome is asserted.

The candidate is bound only to the existing Ute Mountain Ute government profile. The homepage separately describes Southern Ute and northern bands; the proposed paragraph does not merge governments or claim exclusive representation of all Ute peoples.

The homepage has no proposed publication/event date, and current captured bytes equal the October 12 receipt hash. This is an October 15 re-read of unchanged source material, not newly published history or a current emergency.

The proposed paragraph and resource use only the public historical homeland account. No ceremony, sacred content, personal names, contact details, seals, private membership data or coordinates enter the public proposal.
The paragraph opens by attributing the account to the Tribe and links the same public own-publisher homepage. Historical limitations remain visible.
